To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have cloned the coaA15 gene and determined the nucleotide sequence of the gene and that this gene codes for the enzyme pantothenate kinases.
we isolated and characterized temperature-sensitive mutants of Eschericia coli defective in pantothenate metabolism.

we have isolated and characterized temperature-sensitive mutants of Escherichi coli that are conditionally defective in pantothenate metabolism and have localized the mutation to the coaA locus near min 90 on the chromosome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the coaA locus, which is involved in the conversion of pantoyl alcohol to 4'-phosphopantetheine.
the regulation of pantothenic acid metabolism and the isolation and characterization of mutants conditionally defective for coenzyme A biosynthesis.
the characterization and regulation of the enzymes of coenzyme A biosynthesis and the elucidation of the physiological role of coenzyme A.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
coaA is the structural gene of the pantothenate kinases of both Escherichia and Salmonella.
the coaA15 mutation is a missense mutation that alters a highly conserved amino acid residue of pantothenic acid kinase.
pantothenate is converted to coenzyme A in two steps.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have isolated and characterized the structural gene for bacterial pantothenate kinases and that the gene product is a monomeric polypeptide of 35.5 kDa.
we have isolated and characterized the first pantothenate-kinase-defective mutant of Escherichicaoli.
the coaA locus is essential for growth and is the structural gene for the enzyme pantothenate kinases (ATP:4'-phosphopantothenate 4'-phosphotransferase, EC 2.7.1.33).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the coaA15 mutation causes a temperature-dependent inactivation in vivo and in extracts.
the coaA15 mutation is a temperature-sensitive lesion in the pantothenate kinases of Escherichio coli.
the coaA mutants provide a useful system for the analysis of the role of pantothenic acid and coenzyme A in the growth of Escherichica coli.
